ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$, $AB=AD$, $BC=DC$, $\angle B=140^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle D$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$, AB = AD, BC = DC, AC = AC,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle ADC$,\\
$\therefore \angle D = \angle B = \boxed{140^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A is on the left side, C is on the right side, and line segment AC is the common side of the upper and lower triangles; D is located above AC, and connecting AD and DC forms the upper triangle ADC; B is located below AC, and connecting AB and BC forms the lower triangle ABC. Then reason: The problem gives AB=AD, BC=DC; from the figure it can be seen that the two triangles also share side AC, so AC=AC. Therefore the three groups of corresponding sides of triangle ABC and triangle ADC are respectively equal, so ΔABC ≅ ΔADC (SSS). Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal, among which B corresponds to D, so ∠D=∠B=140°.
